articles.headline: Philip Rivers addresses NC State coaching rumors as momentum builds for Wolfpack legend: 'You never say never'
keyFacts: Philip Rivers addressed rumors linking him to the vacant NC State coaching position, stating that nothing is imminent but telling reporters you never say never.
Rivers is currently coaching at St. Michael in Alabama and is focused on the team's upcoming postseason run before any potential future career move.
Reports indicate that Rivers is a leading candidate for the NC State job, while his son Gunner Rivers reaffirmed his commitment to play for the university.
body: There's a lot of smoke around NC State legend Philip Rivers as the Wolfpack search for their next coach. Rivers addressed those rumors on Friday night, but he didn't do much to silence that noise.

Following Fairhope (Ala.) St. Michael's regular-season finale on Friday night, Rivers spoke publicly for the first time since NC State fired Dave Doeren. Rivers said "nothing is imminent" in terms of a deal between himself and the Wolfpack, but he stopped short of denying the rumors.

"NC State is special to me. Coach Doeren, what he did over 14 years, all-time winningest coach, I have a ton of respect for what he did and how he went about it with the university," Rivers told AL.com. "There is nothing there at this point. You understand the chatter that is out there. You take it one day at a time. I'm excited about this postseason with these guys.
"Like I told you last year, you never say never, but there's nothing imminent."

Rivers is in his sixth season coaching St. Michael, where his son and four-star prospect Gunner Rivers is the starting quarterback, and the Wolfpack legend wants to see the season through as the Cardinals prepare for the playoffs. That said, it's hard not to notice the past tense in his answer.

"Shoot, we love it here. It's been awesome," Philip Rivers said. "We've poured everything we have into this program and really looking forward to trying to send this last group off. We've been on the cusp. I know it's a different league, but we've been on the cusp and, hopefully, we can get it done this year."

On the topic of Gunner, he reaffirmed his commitment to NC State on Friday night, which only put more steam on the speculation that Rivers will be the team's next coach. Gunner is the No. 4 quarterback and No. 43 overall player in the 2027 signing class, per 247Sports.
NC State zeroing in on Rivers as coach

It's not much of a secret that Rivers has plenty of support among influential people within NC State circles. CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and John Talty reported earlier in the week that Rivers is the favorite among boosters in Raleigh, and he has a legitimate chance to get the job.
On Friday afternoon -- before Rivers commented on the opening -- 247Sports reported that NC State and Rivers were "closing in on an agreement" to make him the team's next coach.

Rivers played for NC State from 2000-03, and spearheaded one of the most successful runs in team history in the 21st century. Rivers remains at or near the top in just about every one of the school's passing records with 13,484 career yards (1st) and 95 career touchdowns (1st).

The No. 4 overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft, Rivers played 18 seasons in the NFL before retiring and starting his career as a coach. Through six seasons at St. Michael, Rivers boasts an overall record of 55-20 with back-to-back appearances in the state semifinals.

These connections to NC State aren't the first time Rivers has gotten buzz in a major coaching search. He interviewed for the vacant Bills job last year before Buffalo promoted offensive coordinator Joe Brady.

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso speaks after Chelsea's 2-0 win vs Manchester United at Stamford Bridge
keyFacts: Chelsea defeated 10-man Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.
Manager Xabi Alonso's team scored after halftime and converted a penalty following Lisandro Martinez's red card.

body: Chelsea's Xabi Alonso will be pleased at how his Blues stuck to the plan and eventually overwhelmed 10-man Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.
The visitors showed up in better spirits than we'd seen in some time and could've taken a lead into the break were it not for an offside by Matheus Cunha on a would-be goal.

But Chelsea scored after the break and then cashed in a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off around the hour mark. Estevao Willian was sensational and had a goal ruled off for the slimmest offside shortly before a great move was denied by a terrific Senne Lammens save.
The Blues turned into a cruise from there, and Alonso's men moved level with third place Brighton before the Seagulls kicked off at Man City.
Xabi Alonso speaks after Chelsea's 2-0 win over Manchester United
We'll share all of Alonso's reaction as soon as he speaks from Stamford Bridge.

articles.headline: Walmart Gives Surprise Gift Cards Over Canceled Zelda Switch 2 Orders
keyFacts: Walmart canceled pre-orders for the Zelda Switch 2 special edition after overselling the console ahead of its launch.
Affected customers reported receiving either a $519 gift card or the opportunity to reclaim their reservation.
Customers have 48 hours to place their order after reclaiming their reservation, and gift cards are issued within 10 days.
body: On Thursday, Nintendo released a special edition of the Nintendo Switch 2 in anticipation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is set to launch Nov. 5. As with most special hardware releases, the Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary-themed Switch 2 sold out quickly. Walmart oversold the consoles and found itself having to cancel orders a day before launch.
It is now trying to compensate for its actions with $519 gift cards and allowing players to reclaim their reservation for the Switch 2 hardware.

Zelda fans who reserved the special Ocarina of Time Switch 2 for $519 didn't take it lightly when Walmart handed them their money back and canceled their order. Pre-orders guarantee customers that they will get the product on day one. Overselling and canceling orders before launch obviously defeats the purpose of pre-ordering.

The retail chain is now trying to make it up to fans with unexpectedly generous offers. Walmart customers who were affected by the Zelda Switch 2 pre-order cancellations report receiving a $519 gift card in their inbox or the chance to reclaim their order. Gift cards will be granted within 10 days of the initial compensation email. As for the reservation, customers have 48 hours to reclaim it and place their orders, so they must act fast if they still want the console.
Spurned Zelda fans may get their limited edition Switch 2 after all

Most fans have reported that they either received the free gift card or the chance to reserve the special edition console. A small percentage say they got both emails in their inbox, but the majority of the customers were assigned one compensation method at random rather than both.

While it is great to secure an Ocarina of Time special edition Switch 2, the gift card essentially grants what sounds like a free Switch 2 — a deal that almost sounds too good to be true. Either way, it's a win-win situation for the disgruntled customers who lost their pre-orders.

articles.headline: 5 Samsung One UI features you won't get with other Android phones
keyFacts: Samsung Galaxy smartphones feature exclusive One UI capabilities such as Multi Control, which lets users share a single mouse and keyboard across multiple devices without requiring a PC.
The Separate App Sound and Music Share features allow users to route specific app audio to different outputs and let friends connect to Bluetooth speakers through their phone.
Samsung offers advanced customization through the Good Lock app suite and enhanced security protections via Auto Blocker to guard against malware and unauthorized USB commands.
body: 5 Samsung One UI features you won't get with other Android phones
From deep customization to seamless multi-device computing, there's a lot that makes One UI stand out from other Android variants.

Samsung's Galaxy smartphones are the world's most popular Android smartphones, which means that a huge chunk of Android users' experience of the OS is through Samsung's One UI software. But that's not a bad thing: One UI has a slew of unique features you can't get elsewhere, and once you find the most useful features for you, it can be hard to switch to another brand.

Some of Samsung's exclusive features in One UI 9, the most recent version of its skin built on Android 17, can help you use your devices together more easily. Others protect your phone against security threats and advanced malware. But some of the most charming features involve audio. As the owner of brands like Harmon Kardon, Denon, and JBL, Samsung is a major player in the audio space, and its Android skin reflects that with features that let you share and control your music more easily.

All of these features were tested on devices running this year's feature-rich One UI 9 and One UI 8.5, but not every Samsung phone will update to that software. But don't fret: all of these features are also available on One UI 8, which some older devices support.
Multi Control lets you use the same mouse and keyboard with multiple devices

Switching between multiple Galaxy devices — or a Galaxy device and a Windows PC — can be cumbersome. That's where Multi Control comes in, allowing you to connect a mouse and keyboard to one device and use them on the others. Multi Control lets you move your inputs between any combination of Galaxy devices and a Windows PC and use them to control the native Android interface. You can also type in text boxes on all connected devices and even drag files between them.

Other manufacturers have similar features — Lenovo as part of Motorola Smart Connect and Oppo/OnePlus within the O+ Connect suite — but the crucial difference is that those features require a PC to sit in the middle of the connection. Only Multi Control lets you share a mouse and keyboard between a phone and tablet without a PC in the mix. As someone who uses a Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 Ultra as my primary "laptop," this means I can pop my phone on a kickstand, fold out my tablet's keyboard case, and use the keyboard and trackpad to control both devices. It essentially turns my phone into a miniature second monitor, perfect as an always-on Spotify window or a dedicated screen for a calendar or to-do list.

Until recently, Multi Control on PC was locked to Samsung computers such as Galaxy Books. However, as of this writing, Samsung has opened the functionality up to work with any PC. As I write this, my tablet sits alongside my PC monitors, happily accepting the PC's cursor on its screen. My phone sits below the tablet, and I can move my cursor between them seamlessly.
Separate App Sound lets you DJ a party while watching TikTok

Have you ever been in charge of the music on a road trip or at a party and accidentally blasted the beginning of a TikTok or Instagram video over the Bluetooth speaker? If so, Samsung has a feature that will prevent those embarrassing moments.

Android generally wants to play from just one audio source at a time and only to a single output. Playing a video pauses your music, for example, and both will play via the same pair of earbuds. Samsung's Separate App Sound lets you tweak that behavior. You can route apps to specific outputs, so TikTok and Instagram can be set to play through the phone's built-in speaker, even when you're connected to your car's Bluetooth, preventing that road trip faux pas.

To configure Separate App Sound, open Settings > Sounds and vibration > Separate app sound. You will be prompted to pick an app and select an accompanying output device. To go a step further, you can download Good Lock from the Galaxy Store and install the Sound Assistant module. Inside Sound Assistant, you will find the Multi sound setting, which lets you choose which apps can play audio at the same time as other apps. Alternatively, select the "All apps" option to prevent apps from pausing other apps' audio system-wide, essentially forcing Android to handle audio like a desktop OS.
Music Share lets your friends DJ the road trip without diving into Bluetooth settings

We've all been in a situation where a friend wants to take over the car radio to play some of their own music. As eager as you may be to oblige, though, connecting their phone requires fiddling with the inscrutable Bluetooth menus in your car's head unit, which isn't easy while you're parked, let alone while careening down the highway, so you say "no."

Music Share is a Samsung Galaxy feature that solves this exact issue. It allows other devices to connect to your phone and piggyback on your Bluetooth connection. After connecting your Galaxy device to a Bluetooth speaker and enabling Music Share from the Quick Panel, the speaker will show up on other people's phones as "[speaker name] via [your name]." Friends who connect to that device are actually connecting to your phone, which then routes their audio forward to the speaker.

Not just anyone can use your phone as an audio router. By default, Music Share only allows pairing requests from contacts and requires you to approve the connection. You can change these in Music Share settings by long-pressing the Music Share tile in the Quick Panel. Additionally, Music Share will disconnect a device if no audio is played from it for 10 minutes. You can change that duration to five minutes, 30 minutes or never. And, of course, you can kick someone off your Music Share, making it easy to shut a guest DJ down if they abuse your generosity by playing Nickelback.
Good Lock is an embarrassment of customization riches

Nearly every time the topic of Galaxy-exclusive features comes up, so does Good Lock, Samsung's suite of customization tweaks. Good Lock is where Samsung lets its engineers go nuts with features that might overwhelm a basic user. Samsung is already infamous for stuffing its phones to the gills with features and settings most people will never use, so you can get a sense of just how extra Good Lock's additions are. And instead of being a single app, Good Lock is a container for downloadable plugins — 23 at the time of writing — that each enable a bundle of settings.

Home Up, for instance, lets you customize your home screen, while Camera Assistant adds options to the camera app and MultiStar improves multitasking features. Most people have never wanted to replace their home button with a GIF, but Good Lock's NavStar module will let you. Similarly, you may never have thought of setting a longer screen-off timeout for specific apps, but Good Lock has that option tucked away in Display Assistant. Turn app icons on your home screen sideways or make them take up the whole screen? Good Lock can do that. Manually select which camera lens to use? That too. It even lets you reorder your settings menu. Rattling off everything you can adjust in Good Lock would take an entire workday, really.

The best way to approach Good Lock is to download it from the Galaxy Store and start poking around. It's not the most intuitive app, with some functions not clearly labeled and incorrect English copy here and there. But it has a human touch that's often missing from modern tech, and it's clear some features are Samsung engineers' passion projects. The suite is a confusing and expansive tangle of options, but if you love endless customization, it's utterly glorious.
Auto Blocker is an extra layer of security against hackers

Lastly, Samsung includes a suite of security features called Auto Blocker that harden your Galaxy device against the most advanced forms of malware. There is some overlap between Auto Blocker and Google's Advanced Protection suite commonly available on newer Android devices, but Auto Blocker is unique enough to stand on its own. The most security-conscious users should enable both.

Auto Blocker prevents your phone from installing apps sourced from outside the Play Store. While installing apps from anywhere on the internet is one of Android's strengths, those apps can pose risks and contain malware. Auto Blocker also prevents USB commands from reaching your phone. Some attackers use a rubber ducky, a USB stick that executes commands automatically when plugged in. Similarly malicious tools can be hidden in USB ports or cables, which is why you should never use a USB port charger at an airport or other public location. If you do, though, Auto Blocker should make any attack less likely to succeed.

Another feature is protection against malware delivered through a messaging app. With zero-click malware (which doesn't require you to click anything to execute an attack) on the rise, this is another excellent addition to Samsung's security umbrella. Auto Blocker can also turn on automatically after you disable it, keeping you protected even if you turn it off temporarily to install an APK, for example.

If all that isn't enough, Auto Blocker includes another suite of protections in its Maximum Restrictions submenu. When enabled, Maximum Restrictions blocks device admin apps that could remotely execute commands, prevents all USB connections beyond charging, and blocks automatic connections to insecure Wi-Fi networks that could make you more vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. It also blocks 2G network connections, which can be spoofed by law enforcement tools such as Stingrays.

articles.headline: DeSantis suspends Florida mayor charged with COVID-19 fraud
keyFacts: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis suspended Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa following her arrest on felony charges related to COVID-19 grant fraud.
Authorities accused Espinosa of manipulating a city grant program to direct $90,000 to her connected businesses, while Espinosa pleaded not guilty.
Vice Mayor Angela Eady will serve as mayor until the suspension ends or the current term expires, according to the city.
body: Gov. Ron DeSantis (R-FL) on Friday suspended a Florida mayor who was arrested earlier this month on two felony charges tied to allegations of corruption in a local grant program.

Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa was suspended, according to the city, and Vice Mayor Angela Eady will now serve as mayor until the suspension is revoked or until the current mayoral term ends. DeSantis’s order prohibits Espinosa from receiving pay, allowances, or other privileges of office during the suspension.

Espinosa has been accused of creating and expanding a city business program tasked with dispersing COVID-19-era relief grants to enrich herself by the tune of tens of thousands of dollars without disclosing personal interests. Authorities accused her of “systematically manipulating policy and voting on the program just to pave a clear path to her own payout.”

Espinosa was arrested earlier this month, before being issued a public reprimand by the Florida Commission on Ethics and ordered to pay a civil fine of $2,000, after the panel found there was probable cause to believe those grants were illegal. Her suspension by DeSantis comes as, under Florida’s Constitution, the governor has the power to suspend any elected municipal official who has been indicted for a crime or arrested on any charge related to their office duties.

The allegations are tied to concerns that Espinosa created and expanded the Kissimmee Business Boost 2.0 grant program for personal gain by winning $50,000 in grants for businesses connected to her or her family members. In addition, four businesses that pay rent in a building owned by the mayor received a total of $40,000, according to authorities.

Espinosa, who was elected in November 2024, was arrested on Oct. 21 on charges of grand theft and organized scheme to defraud. Her arrest affidavit said the mayor overhauled the grants program as soon as she took office and then was among the first applicants.
She spent the night in jail before posting a $70,000 bond the following day. Espinosa pled not guilty, saying she is innocent and did not act with criminal intent.

Officials have already taken a series of steps to target the mayor. A special prosecutor was tasked earlier this year to interview Espinosa on the allegations. Special prosecutor Mayanne Downs recommended impeaching the mayor in July. The Kissimmee commission voted in August not to impeach Espinosa, after the four commissioner members deadlocked.
She was later issued a public reprimand by a Florida ethics board and fined $2,000.
“She violated section 112, 3137, Florida statutes by having an employment and or contractual relationship with the entity doing business with her agency,” the commission said.

Attorney General James Uthmeier blasted the mayor this month.

“Public officials do not get to write the rules and then write themselves a check,” he said. “Florida taxpayers funded that money to help small businesses recover, not to enrich the mayor who controlled it.”

articles.headline: Chelsea v Manchester United: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Chelsea defeated Manchester United in a Premier League match following a second-half collapse by the visiting side.
Manchester United defender Martinez was sent off in the second half after receiving two yellow cards in quick succession.
Cole Palmer scored a penalty for Chelsea after a VAR review confirmed a foul by Martinez inside the box.
body: 90 min +9: Gusto is slipped into space down the right. He crosses low and long for Barco, who should slam home at the far post, six yards out, but slices his effort off target. It’s not going to matter.

90 min +7: Palmer dances his way into the United box from the right. For a second, things look like opening up for him, but Heaven sticks to his shoulder and ushers the ball out for a goal kick. That’s Palmer’s last act of the afternoon, as he makes way for Quenda.

90 min +4: … so when you’re luck’s out, you’re luck’s out. Manchester United can’t catch a break. That would have been a hell of a goal, but Penders wasn’t having a bar of it! Meanwhile up the other end, Palmer blazes a good chance over. It could have been 2-1; it could have been 3-0.

90 min +2: … and they’re inches away from getting one! The corner’s half cleared to Mbeumo, who shapes like prime-era Zinedine Zidane and absolutely larrups a rising drive towards the top-right corner! The ball caroms off the underside of the bar and out! A sensational shot … and a save to match, because Penders got a fingernail to that, diverting it onto the woodwork! Awesome play all round!

89 min: Mount, formerly of Chelsea, clatters into Palmer and probably should go into the book, but the referee shows mercy. Incidentally, Zirkzee picked up a yellow a couple of minutes ago, for another poor challenge. United have unravelled spectacularly, yet arguably not that predictably, in this second half.
87 min: A triple change for Chelsea. Gusto, Welbeck and Barco come on for Neto, Caicedo and Estevao, who deserved a goal today, but won’t be getting one.
85 min: Estevao jinks in from the right, one-twos with Palmer, and whips a glorious low curler towards the bottom left. Lammens saves excellently. Estevao must wonder how he’s not on the scoresheet.

84 min: Zirkzee has a speculative dig from distance. It’s something, better than nothing, but easy for Penders. Chelsea go up the other end and Estevao’s shot deflects into the path of Lammens. “I’m sure Martinez wants out of this,” writes Tim Stappard. “I wish the rest of them wanted out too.”
83 min: Hats off to Manchester United’s travelling support. They’re chanting their love for this famous old club, loud and long, despite the nonsense unfolding in front of them.

81 min: Mbeumo is booked for delaying the restart as Palmer tries to take a quick free kick. “What was Carrick scribbling away frantically just then?” wonders Andrew Goudie. “His resignation letter?” You could hardly blame him, given the performance of his senior defenders in this second half.

80 min: … Zirkzee should clear, but takes a poor touch and gifts Palmer possession. Palmer aims for the top left, but gets the shot all wrong. “If Zirkzee is the answer, what is the question?” asks rhetoric’s Joe Johnson. “Nothing good, I fear.”
79 min: Palmer wanders past Maguire down the left, way too easily. He crosses for Estevao, who really wants a goal having had two disallowed. He shoots. Deflected. Corner. From which …
78 min: On TNT, Joe Cole suggests that Martinez is “at the scene of the crime too often” and his United career has run its course. It’s hard to disagree.

77 min: Diallo can’t continue. Zirkzee comes on in his stead. “Is it just me or everyone who thinks Martinez is pulling a ‘Romero move’ from last season?” wonders Karen Asad. “It sure looks thay way and a move to Atleti beckons!”
76 min: Diallo goes down feeling his leg. As he gets medical attention, Michael Carrick gives his captain Bruno Fernandes some tactical instruction. The horse already bolted.

This is too easy. Way too easy. Lavia snaffles possession from Fernandes’s loose pass and lays off to Palmer, 30 yards out. He feeds Estevao down the inside-right channel. Estevao lashes a rising shot through and past Lammens, and into the top-right corner.
70 min: Palmer spins around Mainoo. So easy. Mainoo clips him, and goes into the book. Manchester United are being given the runaround now, and are losing their collective composure.

68 min: Estevao finds space down the right and rolls across for Palmer, who would be tapping home at the far stick had Maguire not extended a leg to poke around the post. What fine last-ditch defence.

65 min: “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” trill the Chelsea fans. But can you blame Michael Carrick for such idiocy? “What an absolute idiot Martinez is,” writes Joshua Keeling. “Feel so sorry for Carrick. We played so well in the first half, missed a hatful of chances, terrible defending to give away the first goal, and then Martinez does something as stupid as that. We should have been two or three up at half time, and now look. It’s disgraceful from the players. Not Carrick. The players.”
GOAL! Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United (Palmer 64 pen)
Palmer’s spot kick is no good. Towards the bottom right, but not well hit. Lammens gets a big hand on it, and should stop it … but lets his hand flap back and allows the ball into the corner.

63 min: … a second yellow for Martinez. What an idiotic challenge, one minute and 22 seconds after his first yellow. As Martinez stomps down the tunnel, poor Michael Carrick doesn’t bother looking at his player. You can’t blame him for showing such clear disdain. All that big talk, and now this.

62 min: VAR ushers the referee over to the screen. It’s surely going to be a penalty: Martinez brazenly barged into Fofana. And yes, the ref draws a TV screen in the air. A reckless challenge … a penalty … and …

60 min: Estevao curls the resulting free kick into the mixer, forcing Maguire to head behind. Estevao sends the corner long. Fofana rises at the far stick. Martinez, not looking at the ball but facing his man, barges into Fofana. No penalty … but should it be a penalty? It should be a penalty.
59 min: Rogers ballet-dances his way down the right, a couple of pirouettes sending Martinez into a literal flat spin. Martinez eventually hauls him down and earns himself a booking.
56 min: Estevao tries to chop his way past Dalot down the right, but has to settle for a corner. Estevao takes it himself, and nearly scores directly, but Lammens handles well on his line.

55 min: That was one hell of a goal from Chelsea’s perspective. Lavia broke up United’s attack and started one for Chelsea with a couple of shoogles of his hips. And Rogers’ run, wow. But United’s defence opened up egregiously. Maguire and Martinez not covering themselves in glory.

53 min: A free kick for United out on the left. Fernandes swings a dangerous low ball to the far post, where Cunha inexplicably fails to connect. Anything on that, and it was an equaliser. Fernandes can’t believe he doesn’t have another assist to his long career list.
51 min: Chelsea’s tails are up, and Estevao slides down the right before standing one up for Neto, whose looping header towards the top left is plucked from the sky by Lammens.

Lavia snaffles the ball in the centre circle, seeing off Mbeumo and Baleba in one movement, and flicks the ball to Rogers, who does the rest. Rogers sashays down the inside-left channel at pace, gliding past Maguire with disdain, entering the box, drawing Lammens, and dinking gently over the keeper and in. That’s an outrageous run and finish. Hats off to Lavia too!

47 min: A slow start to the second half, so Stamford Bridge breaks into song in the hope of getting the home heroes going. “That was surely a first half where both teams needed Danny Welbeck as striker,” quips Rick Harris. “Can’t understand why United let him go.”

Chelsea get the second half started. The hosts will be looking for improvement, because Manchester United had the upper hand during that first period: to illustrate, Michael Carrick’s men won the xG battle by 0.28 to 1.01. But there are no half-time changes.

TNT have a quick chat with Michael Carrick before the restart. “We’ve played really well … done a lot of good things … we want to make that count … the game’s always in the balance here … we need to take our opportunities … we need a big second half.”

… and also allow us to introduce our new satire segment, That Was Half Time That Was. “Afternoon Scott,” begins Stephen Carr. “I’d like to take this opportunity to say that Aston Villa are a massive club with incredible heritage and are dead clever and get all the girls.”

I mean … both teams have had a goal ruled out for offside. Both attacks look lively; both defences are a risible shambles. It’s been great fun! We just need a goal. We’re still going to get one or two or five, right? Anyway, here’s the half-time postbag …

“I agree with you, there should be goals in this game, especially given that both defenses are holier than a very tattered shroud of Turin. But conversely, every attacker seems cursed by all the gods of every pantheon. It feels like that if a breakthrough comes it will be an absurd own goal” – Kári Tulinius

“Fans saying that the whole Fernandes (and Martinez) saga wouldn’t have happened under Ferguson need to realise how different the footballing landscape is now. Ferguson was the manager, not the coach, to paraphrase Ruben Amorim. He had full control and final say over everything. If he was in charge today, he would have to answer to the sporting director/director of football etc just like every other coach has to. He would also be subject to the same barrage of abuse that Carrick no doubt has been this week from the respective players agents. Football ‘managers’ have their hands tied behind their back these says; they’re not really in charge of anything - see also Arne Slot and Mo Salah last season” – Dave Estherby
“I know Michael Carrick needs all the help he can get, but having Bruno Fernandes’s brother running the line seems a bit much” – Gary Naylor

45 min: Estevao barges his way down the right and shoots straight at Lammens from a tight angle. He had Rogers clear in the middle. Seconds earlier, Mbeumo nearly got through on goal down the United left. Has a basketball game ever ended 0-0?
43 min: … and now, up the other end, Neto spins Maguire down the left and drags a shot across the face of goal when one-on-one with Lammens. How on earth is this still 0-0?!

42 min: Diallo spins the hapless Fofana down the right and he’s clear! He enters the box, opens his body, and aims a curler towards the top left. Just over. A big miss, though to be fair to Fofana, he got back and nibbled at Diallo to put him off.

41 min: … so having said that, Estevao probes down the right and wins Chelsea a corner. It’s swung towards the near post. The ball clanks off Palestra in slow motion, then off Caicedo, and finally off the right-hand post and away! But it wouldn’t have counted, because the ball hit Caicedo’s arm. All in super slo-mo.

39 min: A corner from the right leads to another from the left. Fernandes loops it in. Colwill wins a header and Penders claims the dropping ball. Chelsea needed that. United have enjoyed 71 percent of possession in the last five minutes.
38 min: Diallo jinks into the Chelsea box from the right and aims for the bottom left. His shot is deflected behind for another Manchester United corner. Chelsea are clinging on at the moment.

36 min: The lead wouldn’t have flattered Manchester United. They’ve been extremely lively in attack; they’ve been the better team. “Has Dr Tottenham retired and handed their practice over to Chelsea?” wonders Sean Orlowicz.
… and it’s just as easily chalked off. Cunha had been nudged into an offside position as Maguire was winning his header. The blood drains from Michael Carrick’s face. When your luck’s out …
Fernandes hits the corner long from the right. Maguire wins a header at the far post. Cunha stoops and guides a header into the bottom right from close range. Easy as that!

32 min: Fofana, who didn’t have a good game at Anfield in the League Cup during the week, allows Diallo to rip the ball away from him on halfway. Diallo steams clear, and enters the box, shooting from an angle on the right. Penders kicks around the post, saving his defender’s blushes. For now …

articles.headline: Iran's supreme leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
keyFacts: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the U.S. and Israel against restarting the war and stated that Iranian attacks would face no geographical limitations.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that there are currently no plans to hold talks with the United States despite ongoing mediator consultations.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported that several oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while using unauthorized routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the U.S. and Israel on Saturday against restarting the war amid weeks of heightened tensions and threats on both sides. He said there would be no geographical limitations for Iranian attacks if the war resumes.
- President Trump said Friday the is "going to end soon," without specifying how, as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to push for a peace deal being haggled over by Iran and the U.S.

- U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper renewed his insistence Friday that Iran's navy has been destroyed and southern shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz are safe and open. His assertion came as Iran claimed several commercial vessels have hit sea mines on that southern route this week.
Iran has no plans for talks with U.S., foreign minister says
Iran's top diplomat on Saturday said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States despite growing concerns over a return to war.

"Currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials, and any speculation to the contrary is merely media assumption," Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.
"We see no need to meet with the Americans at present, our conditions are clear, and the mediators continue their consultations regarding them," Araghchi told Al Jazeera.

Qatari and Pakistani mediators met in Doha, Qatar, on Saturday, where an Iranian delegation was present. Iranian officials, through the Qatari mediators, received an outline for a peace deal from the U.S. last weekend, spearheaded by Vice President JD Vance.

"The American side's attempt to open the door to broader dialogue and understanding is considered a positive step, and if Washington's goal from Vance's message is to stir up differences, it will be a new mistake added to its previous errors," Araghchi told Al Jazeera on Saturday.
Regional leaders call for calm amid fears of new military escalation in Iran

Saudi Arabia's vice minister of foreign affairs said on Saturday the message from the region is that it wants a return to peace. Speaking at a security forum in Bahrain, Waleed ElKhereiji told the audience that efforts were being made to prevent a military escalation and reach an agreement to end the crisis with Iran.

"If you look at … the efforts that everybody is trying to do, the message is very clear. People in this part of the world want to bring peace back to the region," he said. But he said no one can predict the outcome of the efforts.

Concerns are rising about a return to all-out war, especially after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S. President Trump has opined during recent rallies that he could quickly bring the war to an end through military action.
Speaking at the same event, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said an escalation in the region would be extremely destructive.
"We are very confident that … the second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere," he said.
AP/CBS
Iran's supreme leader warns U.S. against resuming attacks
Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, on Saturday warned the United States against launching fresh attacks, amid weeks of heightened tensions and repeated threats.

"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his Telegram channel.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been seen publicly since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in U.S.-Israeli strikes at the start of the war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response."
CBS/AFP
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted "hostile drone" in Riyadh region
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.

"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries." Malki did not say who launched the drone.

In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events.
On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
CBS/AFP
Supertanker caught fire after striking mine in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday that a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of oil struck a naval mine and caught fire while using an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. The Guard said it was the fourth oil tanker to suffer an explosion Friday after attempting to use unauthorized routes through the strait.

Iran has repeatedly warned vessels against passing through the strait without Tehran's permission. It has claimed responsibility for attacks on ships and said last month that vessels attempting to pass through the strait without authorization would face "destruction." Tehran has asserted control over much of the waterway since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Feb. 28.

Earlier on Friday, the Guard's navy said three other tankers caught fire after striking mines in the strait, Iranian state TV reported. It claimed the vessels had switched off their navigation and positioning systems and ignored repeated radio warnings. Iran's report did not identify the vessels or provide details about the crews. The Associated Press could not verify those claims.

Meanwhile, Oman said it had evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged tanker that was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate, catching fire. It is unclear whether that incident is related to the fires described by Iran.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center also reported Friday that a vessel was struck by an "unknown projectile" south of Lavan, an island just off mainland Iran near Shidvar. The organization, part of the British military that monitors maritime safety, said the crew was safe.
Strikes blamed on Houthis target Yemen presidential palace

Yemen's Houthis targeted the presidential palace in Aden on Friday with two missiles, a police official told AFP, hours after Saudi forces said they had intercepted an attack by the group on the Gulf kingdom.
Aden, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognized government, has been targeted repeatedly since Yemen's dormant civil war reignited in July.

Two eyewitnesses told AFP they saw ambulances entering the palace in Aden, a large compound made up of several buildings including facilities used by government and Saudi-led coalition forces, after the incident.
Shortly before, residents and an AFP journalist said they heard two blasts in the city.
The Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa to the north, most recently struck the perimeter of Aden's airport on Wednesday after saying they had targeted a naval base and a military camp last week.
October marks record high for reported strikes in Strait of Hormuz, U.K. navy says

There were more strikes reported in and around the Strait of Hormuz than any other month during the Iran-U.S. war, according to the U.K. Marine Trade Operations Centre, which is supported by the Royal Navy.

There were just over 30 attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman or Persian Gulf reported in October, with only March, the first month of the war, reporting even 30 attacks, according to the UKMTO. There were twice as many attacks in October as there were in September. While there were likely more attacks in the month, the UKMTO only counts attacks reported by verified vessels in the region.

The war also crossed the eight-month mark this week as it started on Feb. 28. Since the war started, there have been 145 reported incidents, the UKMTO said. While the UKMTO does not track who fired the projectiles that hit vessels, the vast majority of strikes came via Iran. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps often claims responsibility for the attacks.
Iran has started to claim a large number of ships hitting mines in the region as well, though they largely do not appear on the list of incidents from the UKMTO.

Since July 6, 59 of the 81 projectile strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region came along the southern route, the UKMTO said. The U.S. has championed the southern route, and used it to escort oil tankers out of the Persian Gulf, while Iran calls the route illegal and says ships need to travel north, along the Iranian coast.
Rubio hosts G20 ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members

Secretary of State Marco Rubio opened talks Friday with G20 counterparts including Russia's Sergei Lavrov, in meetings set to be fractious as wars in Ukraine and Iran, alongside surging energy costs, fan discord.
The foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta takes place just days before crucial midterm elections, setting the stage for a December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Trump's Doral resort.
But ongoing conflicts have deepened rifts even as the United States seeks to focus on economic growth, trade imbalances and supply chain challenges in areas like energy and critical minerals.
Rubio warned at an opening plenary session that the world faces "interconnected economic and geopolitical crises, many of which pose severe threats" to the global economy.
He urged the G20 to work together against threats including strains to global energy and food supply chains, and on freedom of navigation.

Still, few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies — which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France — as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from the conflict with Iran.
Global energy prices have rocketed since U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran from late February triggered Tehran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

"This is the last test case the G20 has, at least under the US G20 presidency, until Miami," Alisha Chhangani of the Atlantic Council told AFP. Its outcomes will affect how the December summit shapes up.
UAE says oil spill from tanker in Strait of Hormuz has been contained

No new oil leakage has been detected from the tanker GEM NO. 2 following an in the United Arab Emirates' territorial waters, as cleanup operations continue along the UAE coastline, the Persian Gulf nation's official WAM news agency reported.

WAM quoted the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure as saying Friday that technical teams had repaired damaged parts of the vessel, restored some operating systems and assessed the ship's structural integrity. Authorities said the source of the spill had been stopped.
According to the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the oil slick is concentrated off Umm Al-Quwain, extending toward coastal areas of Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Sharjah.
Pollution levels have declined, while monitoring and cleanup operations continue.

The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Oct. 9 that a vessel had been hit by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire that was later brought under control. It did not assign blame, but Iran has repeatedly targeted commercial ships in and around the southern Strait of Hormuz, which includes the UAE coastline.
Saudis intercept drone, missile allegedly launched by Houthis
The Saudis intercepted a drone near the capital of Riyadh on Friday afternoon as well as a ballistic missile in southern Saudi Arabia, according to the country's Coalition Joint Forces Command.
The coalition said both were fired by the Houthis. It's unclear exactly where the missile was intercepted in southern Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis have regularly targeted locations in Saudi Arabia, everywhere from just over the border from Yemen to hundreds of miles into the interior, including Riyadh. Airports have been a consistent target of Houthi attacks.
The Saudi coalition had earlier announced it intercepted a drone near the holy city of Mecca, which the Houthis denied was fired by their forces.
Lebanon charges 13 people over seized shipment of Hezbollah explosives

A Lebanese military court on Friday charged 13 people for their alleged involvement in shipping explosives to Hezbollah, a judicial source told the AFP news agency, after authorities seized the roughly 1,100-pound cargo earlier this month.

The charges come as pressure mounts on Hezbollah, long a major political and paramilitary force in Lebanon that the U.S. and Israel consider an Iran-backed terrorist organization. The group has been weakened by back-to-back wars with Israel and is now facing a concerted push from authorities in Beirut, with backing from the Trump administration, to disarm its military wing.
Only two of the 13 people charged over the explosives shipment have been detained, and only eight have been identified, with the remaining five known only by noms de guerre.

Proceedings have been opened "against 12 members of Hezbollah, and one of their spouses," a judicial official told AFP. They were charged with "violating government decisions, possession of arms and explosives, and criminal conspiracy to undermine the authority of the state," the source said.
In a rare admission, Hezbollah acknowledged ownership of the vehicle and its cargo, and even demanded the shipment be returned.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has vowed that authorities "will deal with weapons outside the legal framework with the required firmness."

In June, Lebanon and Israel that included the disarmament of Hezbollah and a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied territory in southern Lebanon, with the Lebanese army stepping in to secure the area.

So far, Hezbollah has flatly refused to disarm or acknowledge the ceasefire, and very little of what Israel calls its occupied "security zone" in southern Lebanon has been handed over to Lebanese forces.
CBS/AFP
Oman evacuates 25 crew members from vessels burning off its Strait of Hormuz coast
Oman's navy has evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged commercial vessel after it was targeted and a fire broke out on board, the Omani Maritime Security Center said in a statement Friday.

The evacuation was carried out in coordination with the Maritime Security Center approximately 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate, the northern tip of Oman that juts out into the center of the Strait of Hormuz.
Crew members were "provided with the necessary medical care," the navy said in a statement.

Earlier Friday, Iran's navy and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said two ships were on fire after striking sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use shipping lanes close to Oman's coast that the U.S. military insists are safe and open, but Tehran considers illegal.
ExxonMobil profits double to $15.4 billion on oil price surge

Major U.S. oil and gas giant ExxonMobil reported Friday that its third-quarter profits had more than doubled to $15.4 billion, as it benefited from higher oil prices and refining margins due to the U.S.-Iran war.
Profits in the period were slightly more than double the $7.5 billion in the year-ago period.
Oil prices have been high since the start of the war. As of Friday, the two main benchmark products, Brent crude and U.S. West Texas Intermediate, remained up about 70% compared to a year ago.
CBS/AFP
Iranian navy claims "enemy drone" destroyed, 2 oil tankers on fire in Hormuz strait
The Iranian navy said Friday that an enemy drone was "struck and destroyed" east of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a statement, the navy also said two oil tankers "were damaged and caught fire after striking naval mines," accusing the vessels of ignoring warnings and navigating in prohibited and unsafe waters with their tracking systems switched off.
It was not immediately clear if the two vessels referred to by the Iranian navy were the same tankers that Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps in the strait.
President Trump says Iran war "going to get wrapped up soon"
President Donald Trump said Friday that the war with Iran is "going to get wrapped up soon."
Speaking to Kansas City radio station KCMO ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, the president said "it's going to get wrapped up soon," without specifying how.
"We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon," he added.
U.S. CENTCOM chief renews insistence that Iran's navy is destroyed and Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes are open

The commander of the U.S. military's Central Command, Adm. Brad Cooper, reiterated his longstanding assertions on Friday that Iran's navy is "at the bottom of the sea" and that southern commercial shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz are clear of Iranian mines and safe to navigate.

In a video posted on social media, Cooper said the U.S. had helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since the summer, while the U.S. naval blockade had prevented Iran from exporting any oil through the strait.
Cooper said he had recently flown over the strait and seen U.S. military "assets in the air and on the water."

"What I didn't see," said Cooper, was Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps "out there at all. They patrolled the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters for decades, harassing and threatening and seizing commercial vessels at will, but they were not out there because Iran's navy is all at the bottom of the sea."

Cooper renewed the claim made by President Trump and the Pentagon since late August that "we also successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognized primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines. And today, U.S. forces remain highly vigilant and present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear."

His comments came a day after Iran's navy claimed four vessels had struck sea mines and been disabled as the attempted to transit the strait via the U.S.-backed southern route. The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said Thursday evening, meanwhile, that a tanker was struck by a projectile in the strait.
It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been hit was one of the four Iran said had hit mines.
Source confirms to CBS News Qatari mediators are in Iran to convey tweaks to latest peace proposal
A source familiar with the ongoing diplomacy confirmed to CBS News that Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday to convey the latest edits to a draft proposal to end the U.S. war with Iran.
The source said there were indications of progress being made.

A draft was presented by Qatari mediators last Sunday, and a response from Iran is expected by the weekend. The aim of the proposal is to avert a return to U.S. military action against Iran, which President Trump has threatened multiple times in recent weeks.
Iran says 2 tankers on "unauthorized route" in Strait of Hormuz had "incidents and were brought to a halt"

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday that two oil tankers had been halted after unspecified "incidents" as they attempted to transit what Tehran considers an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz.

"Two offending oil tankers, one in the eastern part and the other in the western part of the Strait of Hormuz, which were attempting to pass through the unauthorized route, encountered incidents and were brought to a halt in the waters south of the strait," the IRGC said in a statement.
Iran has repeatedly warned shippers that using the southern route through the waterway, which has been promoted by the U.S., puts them at risk as the regime deems it an illegal passage.

The tankers had "switched off all their navigation and positioning systems and, with the support of the terrorist U.S. military, were attempting to exit through the unauthorized route," the IRGC statement said.
The IRGC did not specify the nature of the incidents, which came a day after Iran's armed forces said at least four tankers had been forced to stop in the area after hitting sea mines.

The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said Thursday evening that a tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been hit was one of the four Iran said had hit mines, but the timing of the report suggested it could have been a separate incident.
CBS/AFP
Qatari officials return to Iran to push for peace deal with U.S.
Qatari officials returned to Iran on Friday to push for a peace deal between Tehran and Washington, Iran's state-run IRNA news agency, along with Reuters and AFP, reported.
The talks have been coordinated with the U.S., an official told Reuters.

The delegation is led by a senior adviser to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister and is scheduled to meet with senior Iranian officials, IRNA said, adding that the discussions would focus on bilateral relations between Iran and Qatar, as well as developments in the region.

An official briefed on the latest diplomacy confirmed to CBS News Wednesday that Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Qatar had , and that Tehran would not change its stance on the nuclear issue, something Washington wants included in negotiations from the start.
Tehran wants the U.S. to first lift its blockade of Iranian ports and to drop sanctions limiting the country's gas and oil sales.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday in a post on X that Tehran "continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed" and is working with mediators to review ideas that Tehran included in a proposal floated last month, which was summarily rejected by President Trump but which Iran still wants to see used as the basis for a new ceasefire agreement.

On Thursday, Mr. Trump said a letter from Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei — which was reported by multiple outlets as an attempt to restart peace negotiations — was an outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.
Iran has yet to reply to the letter, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
U.S. military death toll since start of Iran war rises to 23, Pentagon says

The U.S. Department of Defense has added two more service member deaths to its official account of casualties since the war with Iran started more than eight months ago, bringing the overall death toll to 23.

Both of the newly noted deaths on the Defense Casualty Analysis System portal were noncombat related. In total the DCAS portal says 11 service members have been killed by enemy fire during the war, and 12 others have died under circumstances deemed nonhostile, which includes accidents and sickness.

Both of the service members recently added as nonhostile deaths were airmen, including one who died of an illness and another from unspecified causes that remain under investigation, The Washington Post quoted the Air Force as saying.

The two deaths added to the DCAS system are listed under Overseas Operations, which includes deaths recorded by the Pentagon after it for the offensive against Iran in May, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared the operation over.
Saudi coalition says Houthi drone intercepted in Mecca region
The Saudi-led coalition said Friday that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Mecca region fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
"A drone launched by the terrorist Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed in the Mecca region," the coalition wrote in a post on X.
The Houthis denied any attempt to strike Saudi Arabia on Friday, the Reuters news agency reported.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on social media that the group hadn't conducted any operations aimed at Saudi territory, adding that the Houthis only target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.
CBS/AFP
Tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz, U.K. navy says, as Iran claims four ships hit sea mines

A tanker was struck Thursday evening by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center reported, after Iran's navy claimed four ships had struck sea mines in the area.
UKMTO said the ship hit by a projectile was exiting the strait along the southern route, which the U.S. has encouraged international shipping companies to use, when it came under fire.
"There are no reported injuries to the crew or environmental impact … at this time," UKMTO said.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its military claimed in two separate announcements earlier Thursday that four tankers had struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires.

It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been struck by a projectile was one of the four Iran said had hit mines, but the timing of the report from the maritime monitor suggested it could have been a separate incident.
Iran has not yet responded to letter from Vance, Iranian media says

Iran has not yet responded to a letter sent by Vice President JD Vance to the secretary of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, according to the semi-official Tasnim News agency, which is closely affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Tasnim said in a Thursday post on its official Telegram social media account that Tehran was not prepared to drop any of its core conditions for a ceasefire, which include lifting the American blockade of Iran's ports, easing sanctions and giving Iran access to its frozen financial assets held abroad, among other things.

Multiple news outlets have reported that Vance's letter to Rezaei was an attempt to restart peace negotiations, but President Trump said Wednesday that it was a focused outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.

articles.headline: Red Barrels' co-founder is just as confused as we are as to why no one's tried to replicate Outlast's success: 'Honestly, I don't know'
keyFacts: Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin stated that he is confused why other developers have not tried to replicate the horror series Outlast's success.
Morin said that Outlast stands out due to factors like its lack of combat and extreme gore.
Morin added that the studio is happy to remain in a successful niche rather than altering its games to appeal to a wider mainstream market.
body: The Outlast series has been providing horror fans with some of the most grotesque and outrageous scenes for 13 years, and to over 50 million players. The most surprising thing about all of that, though, isn't how it's able to keep players terrified, it's that no one else has tried to capitalise on its success.

Sure, there've been games which have had their fair share of gore involved, Resident Evil 7, Harvester, or Agony are just a few that come to mind. But none of them have either managed to top the gore seen in Outlast and also achieve its continued success.

I decided that no one else would be better to ask about this strange phenomenon than Red Barrels' co-founder Philippe Morin, but he seems just as confused as I am that Outlast hasn't had any imitators: "Honestly, I don't know. Sometimes I ask myself the same thing, but I'm glad that we're still different from other games because it can be so hard. There's thousands games coming out on Steam every year. So that's a lot of other games people can decide to spend time with."

But that doesn't mean the Red Barrels team doesn't get a scare every now and then. "Sometimes there's a game coming up, and we're like, 'alright, this one is probably gonna be the next Outlast'," Morin says. "But so far [nothing's come of them]. It's maybe a combination of different things. The fact that there is no combat or the gore [is lacking]."

My working theory as to why no one has attempted to ride the coattails of Outlast is simply because it's so hard to find the edge of what's acceptable in those kinds of games. Red Barrels has always managed to walk the razor thin line of outrageous horror while managing not to tip over into gratuity that's no longer fun to watch or be a part of. It's a hard task, and one that a mainstream game may not want to gamble with, or a newer studio may not get right the first time around.

Red Barrels has managed to find itself in an incredible circumstance of being experienced enough to truly understand how to push gore to its limits while also being a small enough studio that it doesn't need to break into a mainstream market.

"We're happy to be part of a niche and be successful within that niche," Morin adds. "We don't try to, or I should say, it's not part of our internal dialog that we need to make this more mass market or we need to reach a wider audience. Obviously, we want as many people as possible to play the game, but we don't want to let that dilute or become something that takes our focus away from what makes an Outlast game. If we ever decide that we need to be more mass market, then we'll just come up with a different IP or call it something else."

articles.headline: Lisandro Martinez gets cold shoulder from Michael Carrick after generational head-loss at Chelsea
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off after receiving two yellow cards within 82 seconds during a 2-0 defeat against Chelsea.
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reportedly ignored Martinez as the player walked down the tunnel following his red card.
The defeat leaves Manchester United hovering one point above the relegation zone after winning only one of their opening nine league games.
body: Lisandro Martinez was ignored by Manchester United boss Michael Carrick after getting two yellow cards in 82 seconds against Chelsea.
The defender received his marching orders in a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge after a brainless shove on Wesley Fofana which resulted in a Chelsea penalty.
Carrick refused to acknowledge Martinez on his way down the tunnel AFP
Cole Palmer dispatched the spot-kick to put the Blues 2-0 up, with Morgan Rogers having broken the deadlock early in the second half.
Rogers breezed past Martinez for the goal – and forced the Argentina defender into a clumsy challenge for his first yellow card.
It left Man United heading for yet another defeat amid already intense pressure on Carrick , who appeared to blank Martinez as he headed off down the tunnel.
Carrick was backed by the board ahead of the trip to London , but time is ticking on his time in the dugout.
Martinez in hot water again
The costly red card comes weeks after Martinez called out the United hierarchy in a bombshell interview.
Martinez inexplicably shoved Fofana off the ball
Martinez’s dismissal came moments after talkSPORT’s Stuart Pearce had slammed his second-half display.
“Martinez has lost his head, he’s making some incredible rash decisions,” the legendary former England defender said.
Speaking after the red card, Pearce added: “I’m not sure I’ve seen a worse 20 minutes from a player.”
Is Martinez’s United career over?
Ex-Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole , commentating on the game for TNT Sports , went as far to suggest Martinez’s United days are numbered.
“Martinez, it’s run its course,” he said. “In a Manchester United shirt, he’s at the scene of the crime too often, so I think that’s probably his time done.”
It’s the second time the 28-year-old Argentina international has been sent off since joining United from Ajax four years ago.
Martinez was also dismissed in a 2-1 home loss to Leeds back in April.
His latest indiscretion was emblematic of United’s current plight.
The 13-time Premier League champions have won just one of their opening nine league games this season, losing four.
As such, they find themselves hovering just a point above the relegation zone.

United are also winless in nine matches in all competitions, losing four of their last five, including a humbling 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como – after which captain Bruno Fernandes publicly criticised Carrick’s tactics, resulting in his being dropped for last weekend’s home loss to Bournemouth .
And while fans continue to protest against the club’s owners, the person who will likely ultimately pay the price is Carrick himself.
